_description: xhttptunnel Split-HTTP / Meek Streaming Server Configuration. The psk below is a placeholder that the binary refuses to run with; replace it with a strong random secret, or let scripts/install.sh generate one.

_fields.listen: Server address. Plain address or tcp+udp:// enables H3 only with TLS; tcp:// disables H3 for a CDN HTTP origin.
_fields.target: Default backend service to forward tunnel traffic to (e.g. tcp://127.0.0.1:22 or udp://127.0.0.1:51820). Alias: default_target
_fields.psk: Pre-shared key for authentication. Never sent over the wire: each request carries a fresh nonce plus its HMAC-SHA256 over the nonce, session id and target, so a captured request leaks nothing and cannot be replayed or retargeted. Legacy clients that still send the bare token are accepted during the migration window (upgrade servers first, then clients). Aliases: token, auth_token. Empty = open mode.
_fields.selfsign: Automatically generate simulated Amazon/Bing CDN self-signed TLS certificate if cert/key omitted (set false for plain HTTP behind CDN)
_fields.selfsign_cn: Common Name for auto self-signed certificate (e.g. www.bing.com)
_fields.cert: Optional path to custom TLS certificate file
_fields.key: Optional path to custom TLS private key file
_fields.fallback: Decoy URL to transparently proxy unauthorized requests to (e.g. https://www.bing.com). Empty returns an nginx-style 404.
_fields.allowed_targets: Restrict which targets clients may request. Each entry may be prefixed with 'tcp://' or 'udp://' to restrict the protocol, and is otherwise one of: 'host:port' (exact), ':port' (any host on that port), 'host:' (any port on that host), '[host]' (an IPv6 literal on any port) or '*' (anything). An unbracketed IPv6 literal is rejected because its colons are ambiguous, so write '[::1]:22' or '[::1]' instead. So 'tcp://192.168.1.10:' admits only TCP to that host, 'udp://:53' only UDP DNS, and a bare '127.0.0.1:' admits either protocol. A typo matches nothing rather than widening the policy. Checked at session creation, so a custom Handler only ever sees allowlisted targets. Empty = allow all, including non-loopback hosts.
_fields.max_sessions: Maximum concurrent tunnel sessions allowed on server (0 = default 2000)
_fields.max_sessions_per_ip: Cap concurrent sessions from a single client address (0 = unlimited). Bounds one PSK holder's blast radius; counts the TCP peer address unless trust_proxy_headers is on.
_fields.health_path: When set (e.g. /healthz), expose an unauthenticated JSON stats endpoint on the tunnel listener. Empty = disabled. Keep off on a public listener.
_fields.min_proto_version: Reject (HTTP 426) clients advertising an X-XHTTP-Proto below this. 0 (default) accepts all clients, including legacy header-less ones. Set 2 to force the signed-nonce scheme: a client advertising v2 is admitted only by signature, which closes the bare-token fallback.
_fields.chunk_size_kb: Caps the upstream payload carried by one poll request (clamped 16-900, default 256). Must be raised on BOTH ends together.
_fields.trust_proxy_headers: Honour CF-Connecting-IP / X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP for client-address logging. Those headers are spoofable; enable only behind a trusted proxy that strips them.
_fields.brutal: TCP Brutal (Linux kernel module only; inert on other platforms). Caps the send rate of this server's TCP tunnel sockets in bytes/s. The HTTP/3 socket is never affected. Nested object: enabled (default false; off means setsockopt is never called), rate (bytes/s; 0 is illegal unless bw_exchange supplies one), cwnd_gain (tenths, so 20 = 2.0x; 0 = default 20, max 100), group_id (0 = per-connection only), group_from_remote (derive the group from the peer's address instead of group_id; a static group_id on a server pools every client into one aggregate ceiling), bw_exchange (accept the _BrutalBwExchange protocol), bw_advertise (bytes/s this server can ingest; the peer applies it as its own send rate), bw_interval (seconds between exchange attempts, default 60). Exchange requests are authenticated but do not count against max_sessions. A socket failure never breaks a tunnel: the connection continues uncapped and the failure is logged once.
_fields.dump: Dump raw packet hex data in logs for low-level debugging
_fields.log_level: Logging verbosity: debug, info, warn, error
